control.api_quota.description: **Separate from the sustained rate**, because a nightly sync is a legitimate spike and a flat per-second limit either blocks it or permits the flood it was meant to stop.
**Availability checks and order creation deserve different limits** — one is cheap and polled, the other is expensive and rare.

control.api_version.description: **The commitment, not the intention.** A deprecation policy without a stated minimum is a policy that shortens under pressure.

control.developer_account.description: Where this developer is also a commercial partner. **The link exists and the two are not the same record**, which is what CF-135a was about.

control.integration_listing.description: **Certification expires.** An integration certified against v1 and still listed after v3 is TICVAI vouching for something it has not looked at in two years.

control.sandbox.description: **Always false, and stated rather than assumed** (D2). No cloning, no masking. It is a field so that a future reversal is a visible change rather than a silent one — and because **the whole PDPL and DESC argument for thi

control.webhook_delivery.description: **Truncated, and it is what makes the log useful** — a 500 with the receiver's own error message in it answers the question without a conversation.

control.webhook_subscription.description: **Filtered at subscription, not at delivery.** A subscriber taking every event and discarding 99% is a subscriber the platform pays to talk to.
13.3.22. Tenant, venue, or a business condition on the payload.
**How the receiver knows it was TICVAI.** Without a signature an endpoint accepts a ticket-sale event from anybody who learns the URL.
13.1.29. **An endpoint failing for days is disabled rather than retried forever**, and the developer is told — a queue growing against a dead endpoint is a cost the platform carries silently.

control.footer_config.description: **Required links, held separately from the free-form columns** — a tenant reorganising their footer must not be able to remove the privacy notice by accident.

marketing.invitation.description: **Who pressed the button, which is not always who offered it.** Both are recorded because the allowance belongs to the offerer and the audit belongs to the issuer.

marketing.invitation_campaign.description: **Places held, not invitations sent.** Over-inviting against a known acceptance rate is normal and deliberate; **over-issuing against the quota is not**, and the two must not be the same number.

How many more may be invited than there are places. **A press night invites 150 for 100 seats because 60% come**, and a system that refuses the 101st invitation makes the venue do that arithmetic by hand.

marketing.privacy_incident.description: **The clock starts here, not at occurrence.** 72 hours runs from discovery, which is why this is separate from `occurredAt` and why a discovery nobody recorded is a deadline nobody is counting.
**Or a recorded reason for not notifying.** Deciding a breach is not notifiable is a legitimate decision and an undocumented one is indistinguishable from having missed it.

ledger.event_budget.description: **Purchase orders raised, not invoices received.** The number that tells a producer whether they can still say yes to something.

access.entitlement.description: A ULID, matching `TicketStatus.ticketId` — **stable for the life of the ticket and independent of the media carrying it.** A guest whose wristband broke keeps the same entitlement with a new `mediaCode`.
The definition it was issued against. **Pinned at issue** — a template edited next month must not change what this guest bought.
Who holds it. **Null is legitimate** — a ticket bought as a gift or sold at a till to somebody who gave no details has no subject until it is claimed.
What is scanned — a QR payload, a wristband serial, a card number. **Rotatable without reissuing**, because a guest whose wristband broke should not need a new ticket.

**Not `TicketStatus` — that is a validation result with a misleading name**, computed at scan time and carrying `isValid` and `isInsideVenue`. The lifecycle is `orders.EntitlementStatus`, and `states/entitlement-status.y
**Resolved at issue from the template, then owned here.** A freeze extends it, a reissue replaces it, and neither reaches back to the template.
**The number `validateAccess` decrements and nothing was decrementing.** A ten-entry pass with no counter is a ten-entry pass that admits forever.
Days added by a freeze. **Held here rather than computed from a freeze log**, because a gate has to answer in under 300ms and cannot replay a history to decide validity.
`shareEntitlement`. **The owner keeps it and a second person may present it** — the asymmetry that stops a shared family pass becoming a resale chain.
**How it came to exist, and it matters to finance.** A sold entitlement carries deferred revenue; an invitation carries a marketing cost; a reissue carries neither.
For a reissue or a resale. **The chain is traceable** — a ticket appearing from nowhere is indistinguishable from a fraudulent one.
Where the template carries stored value. **A `retail.Wallet` bound to the entitlement, not a balance on it** (CF-126).

storage.platform.schema_version: Migration bookkeeping. **Written by the migrator, never by an operation**
storage.platform.outbox: **Written in the same transaction as the state change, by the platform, not by an operation.** That is what makes it exactly-once
storage.platform.tenant: read-only projection of control.tenant, outside every cell
storage.platform.sale_board_tile: Child of sale_board_page, which is a child of sale_board. **Two levels down, returned nested**
storage.identity.principal_credential: a credential hash has no response it belongs in
storage.identity.authz_audit: **Written by the authorisation layer on every call**, not by an operation
storage.orders.sales_order_unassigned: Default partition. **No operation names it**; the partition router does
storage.access.scan_event_unassigned: Default partition — rows land here before a scope resolves. **No operation names it**; the partition router does
storage.fnb.delivery_location_outlet: join table. Which outlets serve which locations
storage.fnb.location_code: Rotating, hashed, time-bounded. **Generated by a job, resolved at claim** — never directly created or listed
storage.orders.no_sale_event: drawer opened without a sale. Recorded because it is the classic cover for theft
storage.orders.order_discount: manual discount with reason and approver. Posts to a discount account, never as a price change
storage.orders.payment_tip: tips post to a liability, not to sales
storage.orders.order_media_link: links an order to the media its entitlements were issued onto. What makes append-to-existing possible without editing a paid order
storage.ledger.fx_rate: configured rates with effective windows. A rate change is a new row; the old is never edited
storage.ledger.inter_entity_obligation: what one legal entity owes another after a cross-region redemption
storage.control.cell_cluster: identical cells serving a region. Scaling out is launching another, not growing one
storage.control.tenant_migration: a tenant moving between cells — shared to dedicated, or rebalancing
storage.control.tenant_migration_plan: computed against cell state; expires, because a plan made for a different world is not a plan
storage.ai.provider: Configured providers, models and failover order. Credentials are a vault reference, never a key
storage.ai.policy: What the assistant may do, which roles may use it, what is masked. Resolves tenant then venue (ADR-0018)
storage.ai.conversation: A thread, scoped to a principal and a module. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.
storage.ai.message: Prompt and response with sources, provider, model, tokens and latency. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.
storage.ai.interaction: The audit record. **Retention is unresolved (CF-64)** — a prompt may carry personal data. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.
storage.ai.proposed_action: A draft the assistant produced and a person must approve. Nothing executes from here
storage.ai.knowledge_collection: A collection in the vector store. **One per embedding model** — a collection carries its own vector config and a shard cannot, so two models cannot share one (ADR-0021). Carries the shard key, which is the tenant boundary on shared placement
storage.ai.knowledge_document: Source, status and chunk count. The text and its vectors live in Qdrant
storage.ai.chunk_ref: Maps a Qdrant point id back to its document and scope. **The join between the two stores**
storage.ai.index_source: One declaration per indexed table. The owning service does not know it exists — the AI service consumes the event that service already publishes
storage.ai.index_job: A build in flight. recordsFailed is the number to watch — a source failing on 3% of rows is a search missing 3% of answers
storage.ai.index_entry: Maps a source row to its Qdrant point ids, so a deletion in Postgres can be followed into the vector store. **Nothing cascades between the two**
storage.approvals.request: One request per action needing authorisation. The subject is a reference, never a copy
storage.approvals.decision: Every decision at every level. **Immutable once the request completes** — an approval is evidence
storage.approvals.matrix: What requires approval where. Versioned, because a request must be decided by the rules it was raised under
storage.approvals.rule: Ordered within a matrix. First match wins, so adding a rule cannot silently change another
storage.approvals.delegation: Standing in for an approver. Always time-bounded — an open-ended delegation is one nobody remembers
storage.approvals.escalation: Who was asked, when, and why it moved up. The original approver stays in the record
storage.orders.credit_override: a manual override of a partner credit limit, recorded with who and why. Second table on a marker the deriver only read the first half of
storage.control.release: a shipped version. Promoted through dev, staging and production; superseded by a later one
storage.games.credit_ledger: credits bought, played and won. The arcade equivalent of a wallet
storage.identity.session: **Redis, not Postgres.** `ActiveSession` and `Session` both declare `persistence: none — Redis session registry`, and ADR-0004 makes a session a token with a validity window rather than a row. The schema reference had it as a Postgres table with one column — **a core auth table with nothing in it**, found while chasing Hrushikant's `role_permission` note.
storage.identity.guest_session: **Redis.** `GuestSession` declares `persistence: none — Redis session registry`. Separate from the staff session by lifetime and auth path, and neither is a row.
storage.identity.mfa_challenge: an issued MFA challenge and its outcome
storage.identity.otp_challenge: a one-time code sent to a guest contact point
storage.inventory.stock_level: **Derived from movements, not stored.** `StockPosition` declares `persistence: none — derived from movements`, which is the correct design: **a stored level and a movement ledger that disagree is a stock count nobody can reconcile.** Gating the sale reads the derivation.
storage.marketing.message_delivery: one row per recipient per send. Delivery, bounce and engagement
storage.orders.cash_count_line: a denomination and a count from a blind till count
storage.reporting.report_field: **Generated, not stored.** `ReportField` declares `persistence: none — metadata catalogue, generated`: the fields a report may use are read off the `DataSource` at build time, and **a stored catalogue and a schema that disagree is a builder offering fields that no longer exist.** Retrievable so a report can be found by what it answers.
storage.workforce.rota_assignment: A person expected somewhere at a time. **Not a shift** — a shift is a cash session, and most people on a rota never touch a till
storage.workforce.shift_swap: Both parties agree before the supervisor sees it. Routed through approvals rather than a second mechanism
storage.workforce.attendance: Who actually turned up. **occurredAt and recordedAt are both kept** — a steward clocking in offline is not late because the sync was
storage.workforce.announcement: Targeted by venue, department or role. `emergency` is not a louder `operational`
storage.workforce.announcement_receipt: Delivered and acknowledged, per principal. **The outstanding list is the roll call**
storage.maintenance.work_order_attachment: Photo, video, document, note or signature against a work order. Evidence, not decoration — captured offline and queued
storage.promotions.bundle_choice_group: Pick n from a set. The bundle price does not move with the choice (ADR-0019) — the allocation does
storage.platform.audit_record: **Written by the platform on every write, not by any one operation** (ADR-0022 sits above this). Naming it on 431 lineage rows would say nothing
storage.platform.audit_read: **PII reads only**, written by the platform. Who looked at a passport number is the question a regulator asks
storage.orders.cart: A cart holds leases; an order holds money. Retained after expiry so a recovery link lands on something
storage.orders.cart_line: One line, with the lease that holds its capacity. Null lease for a product with no capacity
storage.catalogue.donation_campaign: Fixed, free or round-up. **Posts to a liability account, not revenue** — money collected for a charity is not the venue’s to recognise
storage.catalogue.waitlist_entry: Who asked to be told when a sold-out session frees up. **Not a queue** — a queue is people standing at a ride
storage.fnb.table_reservation: A booking with a time and a party size. Distinct from a table session, which is a guest already sitting down
storage.orders.donation_line: A donation within a transaction. A line, not a flag, because one transaction may give to several campaigns
storage.control.partner_agreement: Net rate or commission, credit terms, validity. **Versioned** — an order placed last week used last week’s rate
storage.access.parking_facility: A car park and its integration mode. Three modes, and the mode decides what happens at sale (CF-52)
storage.access.parking_entitlement: A guest bought parking. Carries the plate where the mode is plateWhitelist — **personal data**, since a plate identifies a person
storage.ai.layout_draft: A generated seat layout awaiting review. **Ends at previewReady and writes nothing to the seat map** — the draft enters seating.import_job at its existing human commit step (ADR-0020)
storage.qdrant:knowledge: **One collection per embedding model** (ADR-0021) — a collection is the only Qdrant container that can carry its own vector configuration, and a shard cannot. Tenants sharing a model share this collection, separated by shard key and scope_path payload; a tenant forced onto a local model by residency gets its own
storage.orders.deposit_box: A cashier’s cash box. **Allocated to a person, not a workstation** — a cashier moving between tills takes their float, which is what makes a variance attributable. withdrawnTotal reduces the expected close: cash skimmed for banking is not a shortfall
storage.marketing.conversation: A live session with somebody waiting. **Not a case** — a case is a ticket measured in hours, this is measured in seconds. A conversation may create a case; it is not one
storage.marketing.conversation_message: One message. The sender is resolved, never declared, and **the assistant is labelled as one** — a guest talking to a bot that presents as a person is a complaint waiting to happen
storage.marketing.kiosk_assist_session: A staff member acting on a kiosk session remotely (2.1.25). **The guest can always see it and always end it** — assistance a guest cannot stop is surveillance
storage.marketing.agent_availability: Available, busy, away or offline, with a concurrency limit. **Expires** — an agent who forgets to go offline is one conversations queue for
storage.cache:answer: **Question, scope and locale to an answer.** The largest cost lever at a kiosk, where forty questions repeat thousands of times a day. **Invalidated by the same events that invalidate the index** — a cached answer that outlives a price change has misled a guest on the venue’s behalf. **`scope_path` is part of the key**: a cache keyed on the question alone is a cross-venue leak wearing a performance hat
storage.cache:embedding: Content hash and model to a vector. **A tenant editing fifty of twenty thousand chunks re-embeds fifty.** Invalidation is trivial because the key changes when the content does
storage.cache:resolution: Scope and permission resolution, tenant configuration, price lists. **Read on every request and changed rarely** — `resolvePermissions` reads five tables on every authorised call
storage.cache:idempotency: Seen idempotency keys. **Every write carries one as of 17 August and nothing said where the record lived or how long it was kept** — a key store that forgets too early lets a replay through, which is the defect the key exists to prevent. Retention must exceed the longest offline window (ADR-0013) **Retention must exceed the longest offline window** — a scanner out for a weekend replays on Monday, and a key store that expired on Sunday lets every one of those writes through twice.
storage.orders.stored_value_authorisation: A hold against any stored-value instrument (CF-126). **Two-phase spend for all six**, where only the retail wallet had it — a guest with 200 game credits starting a play the machine then failed had no held balance
storage.catalogue.product_version: Version history for a product (BL-030, BL-047, BL-058). **A restore creates a new version rather than rewinding**, so a price that was wrong for three days stays reproducible.
storage.catalogue.import_job: Two-phase catalogue import (BL-057), following seating.ImportJob. **A job that parses zero products is not a parsed job.**
storage.marketing.message_trigger: What fires a message (BL-052). **Before, during and after a visit are one mechanism** with a different sign on the offset.
storage.orders.invitation: A complimentary entitlement issued outside the order path (8.1.3–8.1.5). **No payment is expected, so nothing waits for one.**
storage.orders.invitation_allowance: What a profile may give away and over what period (8.1.5). **An unbounded comp right is how a venue gives away a season.**
storage.marketing.journey: An automated multi-step journey (22.3.1b–22.3.10b, CF-137). **A MessageTrigger is one step of it** — a journey is what you need when the next message depends on what the guest did about the last.
storage.marketing.journey_entrant: A guest inside a journey, at a step. **Pausing does not evict them**, because a half-finished recovery sequence that restarts sends the first message twice.
storage.venuemap.map: A park map or floor plan (19.2.55, CF-123). **Not a seat map** — nothing on it is sold. Published rather than saved, because editing a live map under a guest routes them into a wall.
storage.venuemap.point: What a venue places on the map (19.2.57–19.2.60) — rides, restaurants, toilets, exits. **`emergencyExit` is separate from `exit` on purpose.**
storage.venuemap.path: The navigation graph (19.2.56). **`isStepFree` is the most important attribute on it** — a wheelchair user routed up a staircase was failed by the map.
storage.venuemap.import_job: Two-phase geometry extraction, following seating.ImportJob. **A job that finds nothing is not a successful job.**
storage.resources.resource: A specific bookable object (CF-125, BL-039). **Not a quantity of interchangeable ones** — forty identical strollers are forty resources, because guest twelve returned stroller twelve.
storage.resources.booking: A resource held for a window (BL-040, BL-041). **Setup and teardown sit outside the booking**, which is what stops a calendar double-booking every turnaround.
storage.resources.qualification: What a person resource is certified to do, and until when (BL-042). **A lapsed lifeguard certificate is a safety failure, not a data-quality one.**
storage.resources.session_participant: Who is in a session, in what order (BL-045). **The running order is operational** — an instructor takes beginners first.
storage.ledger.deposit: Money taken before the sale is complete (BL-139). **Not deferred revenue** — that is a sold entitlement not yet consumed, and the sale happened.
storage.orders.payment_provider: A configured gateway (BL-116, CF-131). **Two are confirmed for Phase 1, which is the number that forces an abstraction** — one can be hard-coded and two cannot. Credentials live in the vault.
storage.orders.payment_routing: Which provider takes a given payment (BL-116). **Ordered rules, first match wins, and a fallback that is not optional** — a gateway outage with no fallback is a venue that cannot sell.
storage.orders.payment_token: A stored credential held by the provider (BL-116). **The platform never sees a card number.** Provider-scoped, so a routing change means asking the guest again rather than silently losing their card.
storage.orders.chargeback: A disputed transaction (BL-118, CF-144). **Not a refund** — a bank decides, on a clock the venue does not control, and a deadline missed is a case lost regardless of merit.
storage.orders.fraud_rule: Evaluated before the charge (BL-118). **It holds rather than refuses** — a rule that declines outright turns a false positive into a lost sale with an angry guest.
storage.control.partner_user: A principal on a partner branch (2.7.51, BL-075). **A partner was a flat account.** Quota and credit resolve nearest-ancestor-wins, like configuration.
storage.control.channel_listing: What is published to an OTA (BL-076). **An OTA pulls a feed, caches it and sells against the cache** — so the gap between pushes is the oversell window, and the allocation bounds it.
storage.reporting.alert_rule: Raises an alert when a number leaves a range (BL-152, CF-134). **MessageTrigger seen from the operational side** — a message trigger fires on an event, this fires on a threshold.
storage.reporting.alert: A rule that fired. **Acknowledged rather than dismissed** — an alert that disappears when clicked leaves nobody accountable for what happened next.
storage.marketing.lost_item: A reported or found item (BL-021). **The match between the two is the whole capability** — without both sides modelled, somebody searches a case list by hand.
storage.marketing.referral: A referral code and its reward (BL-034). **The reward is conditional on the referred guest doing something**, not on the referral being sent.
storage.marketing.touch_point: One marketing touch (BL-177). **The platform records touches and does not pick an attribution model** — hard-coding one would make every other unanswerable.
storage.marketing.attribution_touch: Every marketing touch, not just the converting one (BL-177). **A platform storing only its chosen attribution model cannot answer a question asked in a different one.**
storage.fnb.production_run: A batch made for one outlet or several (BL-129). **Production is a stock movement in both directions at once** — ingredients out, sellable items in — and theoretical against actual is the whole point of recording it.
storage.fnb.waitlist_entry: A restaurant waitlist party (BL-130). **Distinct from queue, which is for rides** — this has a party size, a seating preference and a walk-away point.
storage.seating.zone: Standing areas, suites, stages and obstructions (BL-166). **A standing zone is a capacity without individual seats** — modelling it as seats means inventing numbers nobody prints.
storage.orders.resale_listing: An entitlement listed for resale (BL-060). **A resale is a transfer with money attached and the venue stays in the middle** — the seller entitlement is voided and a new one issued, so the ticket that admits is always one the venue issued.
storage.orders.ticket_template: Ticket artwork and media selection (BL-102). **A venue changing its artwork had no path that was not a code change.**
storage.games.reader_profile: How a game reader behaves and what it shows (BL-153). **A guest at an arcade machine cannot read a message, they can only see a light.**
storage.control.content_block: Authored content with a schedule (BL-172). **The CMS modelled configuration and not authoring** — a marketer could choose between things a developer had built and could not write something new.
storage.control.onboarding_application: A prospect signing themselves up (BL-165). **Nothing is provisioned until verification passes** — an unverified application that provisions a cell is a cell somebody has to clean up.
storage.control.venue_type_template: What a venue of this kind starts with (BL-165). **A water park and a theatre need different defaults**, and configuring 300 settings from empty is asking a prospect to leave.
storage.inventory.stock_batch: The instance that actually expires (BL-122). **isPerishable and shelfLifeDays are on the item, so a shelf life was declared and never instantiated** — two deliveries a week apart were one stock level with one implied expiry.
storage.orders.group_booking: A group with a leader and an attendee manifest (BL-028). **A school booking forty places has one person who pays and forty who need names collecting**, and a generic order has one guest.
storage.orders.wallet_pass: An Apple or Google wallet pass (BL-029). **A live object, not a download** — a pass that cannot be pushed to is a screenshot with better rounding.
storage.marketing.challenge: A challenge, mission or streak (22.6, CF-137). **Gamification is not loyalty** — loyalty pays for spend, a challenge pays for behaviour spend does not produce.
storage.marketing.challenge_progress: How far a guest is (22.6.15). **Progress is shown, not just the outcome** — a guest two visits from a reward behaves differently from one who does not know.
storage.control.seo_metadata: Titles, canonicals, hreflang and schema markup (22.11). **An attraction that does not appear in search sells through OTAs at OTA commission.**
storage.control.url_redirect: 301s and 302s for retired content (22.11.7). **A redirect chain loses ranking at every hop**, so a new one pointing at a redirect is collapsed.
storage.marketing.form_definition: A waiver, survey or capture form (CF-129). **One mechanism, three uses** — three implementations would drift on the version rule first.
storage.marketing.form_submission: The acceptance record, and it is evidence (2.15.13). **Bound to the version accepted, not to the form.**
storage.marketing.guest_document: A guest photo, ID or signed document (BL-133). **Deliberately not assets** — a passport scan is not a marketing asset and has a different retention clock.
storage.identity.password_policy: Length, breach check, lockout and step-up (BL-144). **Modelled on NIST SP 800-63B rather than habit** — length beats composition, and forced rotation makes passwords worse.
storage.identity.segregation_rule: Which permissions may not be held together (BL-147, 3.3.31). **Checked at grant time, not use time** — discovering the conflict when somebody exercises it means it already existed.
storage.control.developer_account: A developer organisation (13.1.6–13.1.9). **An organisation, because an integration outlives the engineer who built it** — and not a tenant or a partner.
storage.control.api_client: The one credential model (CF-135a). **2.7.52, 7.1.25 and 7.1.30 each asserted their own.** Bound to one environment, because a key that works in both is a key somebody will use in the wrong one.
storage.control.sandbox: A developer sandbox (13.2.1, D2/D3). **Synthetic data only** — no cloning, no masking, which removes the PDPL and DESC exposure entirely.
storage.control.webhook_subscription: An external subscriber to business events (13.1.26, 13.3.18). **The 29 events existed and nothing outside could receive one.**
storage.control.webhook_delivery: What was sent and what failed (13.1.30). **The log a developer needs most** — without it every question is a support ticket.
storage.control.api_quota: Rate limits per client (13.1.36). **A quota protects the venue, not the developer.**
storage.control.api_version: API versions and sunset dates (13.1.31–35, ADR-0031). **With third parties a breaking change with no window breaks somebody else business.**
storage.control.integration_listing: A published third-party integration (13.1.50). **A listing, not an installation** — the code runs on the developer own infrastructure.
storage.control.api_licence: Which API modules a tenant licensed (13.3.24, D5). **Configuration, not code** — rates change without a release.
storage.control.footer_config: Footer columns and legal links (BL-002). **A header is chrome and a footer is a link surface** — legal links are held separately so a tenant cannot remove the privacy notice by accident.
storage.marketing.invitation_campaign: A quota-bounded addressed invitation (BL-150). **A campaign broadcasts; an invitation expects a response.** quota is places and overInvitePercent is invitations.
storage.marketing.invitation: One addressed invitation with a single-use token (BL-150). **A link forwarded to a group chat is the failure mode.**
storage.marketing.privacy_incident: A personal-data breach (BL-176). **UAE PDPL gives 72 hours from discovery** — discoveredAt starts the clock, and a discovery nobody recorded is a deadline nobody is counting.
storage.ledger.event_budget: What an event cost against what it earned (BL-049). **Profitability is revenue minus committed cost** — an event three weeks out with purchase orders raised has spent it.
storage.access.entitlement: **What a guest actually holds** — found missing 18 August. The package sold products, defined EntitlementTemplate, recorded ScanEvent.ticketId, transferred ticket_ids and issued wallet passes against entitlementId: **five artefacts referring to a thing that did not exist.** validateAccess read the template and suspendEntitlement suspended it, **which would have suspended it for every guest who held one.**
storage.platform.denomination: Cash denominations per region (Tanmay, review 20 August). **isActive is the field that makes this a table** — a note withdrawn from circulation is deactivated and stays in the count history, and a JSON blob cannot deactivate anything.
